Counterevidence: Repeated source/target vertices and distinct parallel edges with the same vertex tuple are explicitly allowed by Remark2.2.
Counterevidence: Definition2.5 explicitly permits one generic tensor reused by permitted permutations; independent tensors per edge are only one possible partition.
Counterevidence: Definition2.6 does not exclude isotropic vectors. Remark2.4 specifies the bilinear contraction under which (1,±i) are isotropic.
Counterevidence: No exceptional tensor or symmetry condition is imposed: existence holds for everyT.

Counterevidence: The counterexample does not invalidate all classical single-tensor special cases or the formal Chern-class calculation. It invalidates the stated arbitrary-hyperquiver conclusion and related proof step.

Counterevidence: The rank(B_i)>dimY_i inequality appears only in the additional part(b) conclusion, not in Definition5.2 or part(a)/(c). Remark5.4 explicitly confirms its removal from the earlier definition.

Counterevidence: The explicit stratum data verify the intended 'almost generated by Lambda' requirement; the fact that the bundles also possess other generating subspaces does not repair the theorem for thisLambda.

Counterevidence: Friedland–Ottaviani arXiv1210.8316v3 Definition5 p.10 includes rankE_j>dimY_j, and Theorem6 p.11 excludes the bad locus using that inequality. Our counterexamples violate the earlier stricter inequality and therefore do not refute the cited result.

Counterevidence: Requiring global generation by the actualLambda would remove these examples, but a complete repaired theorem and its applicability to every hyperquiver in the paper have not been established here.
Counterevidence: Neither example alone refutes the generic eigenline or singular-vector count in Theorem 3.1; those familiar matrix counts remain correct.

Counterevidence: Theorem 5.3 is formulated for a subspace Lambda of sections, and Proposition 6.7 explicitly uses Lambda=im(L_F). The final main-theorem proof (PDF pages 30-31) invokes Theorem 5.3, Proposition 6.7 and Proposition 7.1 rather than requiring bijectivity of Proposition 4.5.
Counterevidence: A linear parameter map is surjective onto its own image, so a generic parameter can be treated as a generic image section without assuming injectivity.

Counterevidence: The definition explicitly identifies classes only up to scaling; the example above already counts projective classes, so infinitely many scalar representatives do not explain the discrepancy.
Counterevidence: Restricting to simple spectrum repairs the zero-dimensional eigenline conclusion, but it gives dim(H_k(X)) eigenlines, not one.
Counterevidence: The identity example is nongeneric and is used only against the unconditional dimension assertion, not against a correctly restricted generic theorem.
Counterevidence: The update has two eigen-directions, but existence/counting of fixed directions does not imply attraction of arbitrary starts.
Counterevidence: The counterexample does not use zero outputs, an undefined projective direction, asynchronous scheduling or an ambiguity in the update order.
Counterevidence: If the prose were explicitly conditioned on a convergent trajectory, the issue would be narrower; the rendered statement is unconditional.

proposition.claim:
For every hyperquiver representation generic in Definition2.5, Theorem3.1 asserts emptiness if N<0, and otherwise, when the prescribed coefficient D is nonzero, smooth pure dimensionN and degreeD.

Theorem5.3(a) states generic emptiness for rankB>dimX under Definition5.2 almost generation; part(c) states the generic zero locus is empty or smooth of pure expected dimension when rankB<dimX.

Proposition 4.5 asserts that L from one tensor parameter space per partition block to the full global section space Gamma(B(R)) is bijective.

For arbitrary compact triangulable X,P and continuous f:X x P -> X, the example asserts dimension d-1 for the fixed-homology singular variety and states that connected P gives exactly one nonzero fixed homology class, up to scaling.

The multilinear update steps are asserted to converge in the limit to a fixed point without a stability or spectral hypothesis.

repair.content:
No corrected universal hyperquiver theorem is asserted. Repair would require a genuinely justified hypothesis or stratum analysis controlling the extra dependent edge equations; simply adding the incorrect p.31 rank assertion is insufficient.

No full replacement theorem supplied. Keep the earlier rank restriction and generic smoothness hypotheses explicit in any attempted repair, then prove applicability separately.
